transcript:
Header: Date: 2026-02-25 · Start: 15:00 UTC · Duration: ~48m
Attendees: Jenna Ortiz (Redwood AE), Marco Liu (Redwood SE), Sofia Kim (Redwood CSM); Priya Sharma (Polaris Head of Platform), Liam O'Connor (Polaris SRE), Renee Park (Polaris Security), Diego Alvarez (Product)

Summary: Quick onboarding sync to align on marketplace packaging, authz/KMS pattern for private connectors, and LLM routing/fallback behavior for the Polaris connector. Agreed to run a short perf lab and share listing assets. Some discussion around dedicated vs hosted capacity and telemetry requirements.

Topics: marketplace manifest, VPC/private connector, KMS integration + key rotation, RBAC and audit logs, routing policies (latency vs cost), fallback model variants, bench plan, canary/rollout strategy, telemetry retention limits.

-- Transcript --
[00:00] Jenna Ortiz: Okay, uh, thanks everyone for joining, um, we'll keep this to 45ish minutes. Jenna from Redwood, I'm the AE owner on this. Marco from our SE team will drive the tech lab part. Sofia is on for CSM stuff.
[00:12] Priya Sharma: Hi all, Priya here. Quick context: Polaris is building an LLM gateway that routes customer requests through external connectors. We want to list a Redwood-backed connector in the marketplace so customers can deploy using our managed flow or our VPC connector. Key asks are security, low latency, and clear billing for per-token costs.
[00:29] Marco Liu: Thanks Priya. Quick clarifying q — when you say "VPC connector" are you thinking we host a private control plane or you want a direct VPC peering option?
[00:40] Liam O'Connor: Sorry, Liam — we want VPC peering initially, basically customer-owned network with a private endpoint that talks to Redwood dedicated infra. No control plane handover.
[00:50] Jenna Ortiz: Got it. That maps to our Private deployment pattern where control plane is customer-managed but infra is Redwood-managed? Marco correct me if I'm wrong.
[00:59] Marco Liu: Yeah so we have two flavors: Private (VPC + Private connector) where the control plane is still hosted but network egress is via customer VPC peering or we can do on-prem package for fully air-gapped. For marketplace listing, most customers pick the VPC-enabled connector for ease.
[01:15] Renee Park: From security: we need KMS integration and clear key rotation docs; also wanting assurance around audit logs and token retention. Do you support HSM-backed keys?
[01:26] Marco Liu: We integrate with customer KMS via an encrypted envelope approach — we can support AWS KMS, GCP KMS, and customers can use HSM via CloudHSM if they need it. Key rotation is supported, but note there are cache side effects for older KV caches during rotation — we should document TTL behavior.
[01:45] Priya Sharma: When you say KV cache side effects, can you explain? Our concern is that during rotation we might see increased latency because caches are invalidated.
[01:53] Marco Liu: Right — if you rotate keys and re-encrypt prefix caches we may drop some cache entries. The runtime has a rolling-rekey path but there can be transient cache misses causing a few ms to hundreds ms extra per token depending on seq len and batch. We'll add that into the bench plan.
[02:12] Diego Alvarez: Also curious about routing. Polaris wants to route by tenant: e.g., prod traffic to Redwood dedicated low-latency pool, dev to cost-optimized hosted models. But want automatic fallback when capacity is low. Can Redwood do that routing policy?
[02:28] Marco Liu: Yes, routing policies are policy driven. We've got rules for latency-first, cost-first, region affinity. Fallbacks can be model-variant based; e.g., if full fp16 model unavailable we'll route to a quantized 4-bit variant with configured quality thresholds. There is some art to tuning quality numbers.
[02:44] Priya Sharma: Hmm that fallback worries product — we can't silently change model behavior for prod requests. Need guardrails and observable diffs.
[02:52] Sofia Kim: Absolutely — we surface Quality Regression Alerts and allow you to tie a prompt set/eval so fallback triggers only if model quality delta within X% on your eval set. We also expose per-route traces for every request so you can audit which model served the response.
[03:12] Liam O'Connor: Good. What's the latency cost delta between full model and quantized fallback typically? We need P99 numbers to decide.
[03:20] Marco Liu: Ballpark — for an MPT-style 13B, full fp16 p99 could be ~180ms on our dedicated pool, 4-bit quant might rise to 220ms but cost drops 40-60%. Those are example numbers, obviously hardware and seq len change it. We should run your payloads through our lab to produce concrete numbers.
[03:40] Priya Sharma: Perfect. We'll share sample prompts and token histograms.
[03:46] Jenna Ortiz: On marketplace packaging, we have a manifest template that includes listing copy, icons, terraform snippet for connector install, and a security checklist. We'll send that after the call.
[03:56] Priya Sharma: For the terraform, can it provision the peering and the IAM roles? We want the least friction.
[04:03] Marco Liu: Yes, the terraform sample can create peering and IAM service account with limited scopes. It doesn't create KMS keys — we make that explicit — you create the CMKs and grant Redwood principal access.
[04:16] Renee Park: For compliance, we need SOC2 + ISO docs and a data retention SLA. Is the audit log retention configurable per account?
[04:25] Marco Liu: Configurable within limits. We have 90, 365, multi-year+ packages but longer retention is an add-on due to storage. Audit logs include per-token tracing and route info, but we can redact payloads based on customer policy.
[04:44] Diego Alvarez: There's also an operational concern — can we do canaries? Like first 1% traffic to new connector, then 10 etc with automatic rollback?
[04:53] Marco Liu: Yes, rollout support exists. Canary percentages, linear ramp, and automatic rollback on latency or error thresholds. You can gate on quality eval or error rate.
[05:05] Priya Sharma: About telemetry, what fields are included in trace? We want request id, tenant id, model id, latency buckets, and attachable debug KV traces.
[05:15] Marco Liu: That's correct. We include request id, route id, model variant, region, p50/p95/p99, and you can opt-in to full KV debug traces for a subset of requests. Those are redacted by default.
[05:31] Liam O'Connor: Ok, back to marketplace listing — what's the approval flow? We don't want our listing blocked by missing security docs after we go to publication.
[05:40] Jenna Ortiz: There's a preflight checklist: listing manifest, basic security attestation, privacy + SLA doc. Once the checklist is green our listing moves to staging for one week of traffic validation. We can accelerate for partners with a dedicated partner intake.
[05:58] Priya Sharma: We also have a concern about cost transparency — customers will be billed per token plus a connector service fee; we need clear pass-through cost lines.
[06:08] Sofia Kim: We provide a cost breakdown tile in the console and marketplace listing shows estimated per-100k tokens cost. Billing connectors can be configured as pass-through or include a reseller margin.
[06:20] Diego Alvarez: Any constraints on model weights or quantization licensing we should show on the listing?
[06:26] Marco Liu: If it's a third-party open model with a license that disallows quantization, we flag that. Most open models are fine but we include a model licensing section in the manifest.
[06:37] Priya Sharma: For the perf lab — technical ask: can you run with our token histogram and also simulate TLS overhead and VPC hop? That's often where p99 balloons.
[06:47] Marco Liu: Yes we'll simulate VPC egress and TLS handshake cost, and we can include an additional 50–100ms synthetic network tail if you expect cross-region peering. We'll outline assumptions in the bench sheet.
[07:05] Renee Park: A question on encryption in flight: do you terminate TLS at Redwood or keep end-to-end to our peered endpoint?
[07:13] Marco Liu: TLS terminates at our edge if you're using hosted control plane. For VPC peering, traffic stays within peered network and TLS can be end-to-end to the peered endpoint — there are multiple patterns. We'll include recommended patterns in the KMS + network docs.
[07:29] Priya Sharma: Great — I want to make sure rollback and incident playbooks are in place. If a model regression slips through a canary, what's the fastest path to mitigate?
[07:39] Marco Liu: Fastest is automated rollback to previous model variant plus disabling the connector route, and we have a hotfix path where we re-route traffic to a fallback model in under a minute. We also support on-call hooks and pager integrations.
[07:57] Liam O'Connor: Regarding SSO/SCIM for admin access to listing telemetry, is that a separate tenant mapping?
[08:04] Sofia Kim: No, we map SCIM groups to RBAC roles during onboarding and you can assign telemetry viewers vs admin. We'll share SCIM mapping docs.
[08:12] Priya Sharma: Good. Any known gotchas?
[08:16] Marco Liu: A few: 1) Key rotation + cache invalidation as mentioned; 2) quantized fallback sometimes changes tokenization behavior slightly — affects exact-match QAs; 3) VPC cross-region peering can cause unexpected tail latency. We'll highlight these in the manifest.
[08:33] Priya Sharma: Sounds reasonable. We're aiming to have listing live mid-March if all goes well.
[08:39] Jenna Ortiz: Awesome. Recap of immediate items — we'll send listing template + security checklist; Marco will schedule the perf lab and provide bench sheet; Priya will share token histograms and SLOs; Renee will confirm compliance gaps.
[08:55] Diego Alvarez: One final: any partners program incentives or co-marketing for early marketplace listings?
[09:01] Jenna Ortiz: Yes we have a partner early-listing program for joint PR and featured placement — that's handled by our partnerships team, I'll introduce you to them.
[09:10] Priya Sharma: Thanks, we'll follow up after we review the materials.
[09:14] Jenna Ortiz: Thanks everyone, we'll send notes and action items.

End of call.
